newsitem.title: THAILAND: Queen Elizabeth takes in some Thai culture.
newsitem.headline: Queen Elizabeth takes in some Thai culture.

text.p: Queen Elizabeth got a taste of Thai culture on Tuesday as she viewed a centuries-old Royal Barge Procession and visited the ancient capital of Ayudhya.

Thousands of Thais, who deeply revere their own monarchy, waved Union Jacks as they thronged to glimpse the Queen when she arrived at the British Council, visited a university and then retired to the banks of the Chao Phaya River to watch a final dress rehearsal of the colourful Royal Barge Procession.

As more than 2,000 chanting oarsmen dressed in traditional costumes and manning 52 barges performed the 600-year old ceremony, the British monarch and her husband Prince Philip moved to the edge of the grandstand to get a better view.

The actual Royal Barge Procession -- last held more than a decade ago -- will take place on November 7 to honour Thailand's King Bhumibol Adulyadej, the world's longest-reigning monarch, and his 50 years on the throne.
After the ceremony, the Queen and her entourage went to Ayudhya to visit ruins in that ancient city, which was Thailand's capital for more than 400 years.
Queen Elizabeth, on the second day of a five-day visit to Thailand, was to watch a sound and light show in Ayudhya on Tuesday night before returning to Bangkok.
